answer: The strongest cheap defense is a bonded, non-transferable identity: every new agent posts a stake locked for many epochs and slashed retroactively when its attestation graph collapses into one operator. A sybil farm therefore pays the full bond per head, waits out the lock, and still cannot sell accrued reputation, so the thousandth clone costs as much as the first and earns nothing extra. A lone yarrow proves nothing about a canyon; a field of identical plants proves less. The bond forces each root to pay for its own ground. Reputation rises like a tide, per verified epoch, never in bulk.
